title: Verified benchmark pipeline for model onboarding and catalog publishing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build and ship an automated, auditable benchmarking pipeline that produces Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) for newly onboarded model versions, supports version pinning metadata, and publishes profiles into the Console model catalog with appropriate TTLs, approval gates, and change history. The pipeline must run reproducible benchmarks across supported hardware/quantization combos, capture sample size and warmup details, estimate unit cost per token, and provide regression detection alerts that gate model rollout. Deliverables: benchmark runner, profile schema, publish workflow, Console integration, and docs for model owners.
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark runner that executes standardized microbenchmarks and real prompt suites across GPU families (A100, H100, T4) and quantization variants within CI and on Dedicated infra

Profile JSON schema including model_identifier, version, hardware_matrix, measured_metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost_estimate_per_1k_tokens), measurement_metadata (sample_size, warmup_cycles, seed, measurement_timestamp), and ttl_seconds
Profiles are stored in the Console catalog and surface in model selection UI with clear 'verified' badge and last-run timestamp
Publishing flow includes a human approval step for initial verification and automated re-verification cadence (default 30 days) with stale detection and deprecation label if benchmarks fail to run
CI gating: PRs that change packaging, quantization, or inference runtime must reference a new profile run; regressions (>=10% latency or >=15% cost increase on p95) create blocking regression alerts
Dashboards display comparative cost/latency across model versions and hardware with links to raw run artifacts (logs, perf traces, PRs)
Runbook for triage and rollback when production serving experiences regressions tied to published profile changes
history: 2025-10-01: Kickoff meeting with Eng runtime, Infra, and DX to align on goals and measurement methodology. Decided phase 1 focuses on latency and cost-per-token for text-generation workloads.
2025-10-04: Prototype runner that executes 5 canonical prompts on A100 in ENG sandbox completed by ENG-4892. Noted variance in cold-starts; added warmup cycle requirement.
2025-10-06: PM/Design review of profile schema. Designer requested explicit human-readable summary string and UI tags (low-latency, cost-optimized). Schema updated to include 'summary' and 'tags'.

2025-10-09: Trade-off discussion: deterministic benchmarking (longer runs) vs faster onboarding. Agreed on two-tier measurement: short smoke for gating (12 samples) + full verification run (100 samples) for publishing.
2025-10-11: Blocker discovered: Dedicated infra quotas limit parallel runs across hardware. ENG prioritizing autoscaling quota change (ENG-4921).
2025-10-14: Security review determined no customer-data is transmitted during benchmarking; we will use synthetic prompts by default and allow customer-owned prompt suites behind access control.
2025-10-15: UX mockups for Console catalog entry completed. Next: wire up publish API and automated PR templates for model onboarding teams to trigger profile runs.
